rationale: The profile gives no function-level features (no source lines, no function list), so the table must be robust for an unknown, likely small C++ program from Prolangs-C++ 'family' — presumably arithmetic/logic-heavy but not performance-critical, since it is a benchmark toy. I prioritize reverse-engineering resistance: SUB and BCF get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with low CorrectnessRisk because they are well-hardened, semantics-preserving passes suitable as a baseline for unknown code. FLA and SPLIT add control-flow flattening and basic-block fragmentation with moderate cost weights, letting the selector apply them where functions have enough blocks to benefit without bloating tiny functions. IBR and ICALL are weighted high on SecurityGain because indirect branching and indirect calls are among the strongest static-analysis and call-graph-defeating transforms, but their elevated RuntimeCost and CorrectnessRisk weights keep them away from hot or fragile (e.g., vtable-heavy C++) paths; IGV is included at moderate weight since a small program has few globals, limiting both its benefit and its downside. Overall the cost and risk weights sit below the gain weights, so the selector favors obfuscation for feature-matching functions while still excluding hot loops and correctness-sensitive code.
